2	## Writes the prototype's placeholder sprites as PNGs. Every pixel comes from this code:
3	## flat cartoon colours plus a dark outline, no generated or downloaded art.
4	##   godot --headless --path godot --script res://tools/make_sprites.gd
5	
6	const OUTLINE := Color("2b2b2b")
7	const OUT_DIR := "res://assets/sprites/"
8	
9	# Named colours, so later work (shader predictions) can refer to exact source values.
10	const STRAW := Color("e9c46a")
11	const BURLAP := Color("d9b98a")
12	const POLE := Color("8b5a2b")
13	const HAT := Color("7a4e2d")
14	const PATCH := Color("b5651d")
15	const HOOD := Color("3a7d44")
16	const SKIN := Color("f1c27d")
17	const BOW := Color("6b3e1f")
18	const LEATHER := Color("5a3a22")
19	const CHEST := Color("9c6b3c")
20	const LID := Color("7a4e2d")
21	const GOLD := Color("e2b33c")
22	const WHITE := Color("f7f3e8")
23	const FLAME := Color("ff7a1a")
24	const STEEL := Color("9aa3ab")
25	const FLETCH := Color("c0392b")
26	
27	
28	func _init() -> void:
29		DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(OUT_DIR))
30		_save(_scarecrow(), "scarecrow.png")
31		_save(_archer(), "archer.png")
32		_save(_arrow(), "arrow.png")
33		_save(_mimi(), "mimi.png")
34		_save(_scarecrow_walk(), "scarecrow_walk.png")
35		quit(0)
36	
37	
38	func _save(img: Image, file: String) -> void:
39		var err := img.save_png(OUT_DIR + file)
40		print("%s %s %dx%d" % ["wrote" if err == OK else "FAILED", file, img.get_width(), img.get_height()])
41	
42	
43	func _scarecrow() -> Image:
44		var img := _blank(56, 72)
45		_scarecrow_parts(img, 0, 0)
46		return _outlined(img)
47	
48	
49	## The scarecrow's flat parts (no outline) with its 56x72 frame's top-left at (ox, oy).
50	func _scarecrow_parts(img: Image, ox: int, oy: int) -> void:
51		_rect(img, ox + 26, oy + 30, 4, 40, POLE)            # pole
52		_rect(img, ox + 4, oy + 30, 48, 4, POLE)             # cross-stick arms
53		_rect(img, ox + 2, oy + 28, 5, 8, STRAW)             # straw tufts at the hands
54		_rect(img, ox + 49, oy + 28, 5, 8, STRAW)
55		_ellipse(img, ox + 28, oy + 46, 14, 16, STRAW)       # straw-stuffed body
56		_rect(img, ox + 31, oy + 45, 6, 6, PATCH)            # sewn patch
57		_ellipse(img, ox + 28, oy + 22, 11, 11, BURLAP)      # sack head
58		_rect(img, ox + 12, oy + 12, 32, 4, HAT)             # hat brim
59		_rect(img, ox + 18, oy + 2, 20, 11, HAT)             # hat crown
60		_rect(img, ox + 23, oy + 20, 3, 3, OUTLINE)          # eyes
61		_rect(img, ox + 31, oy + 20, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
62		for x in range(23, 34, 2):                           # stitched mouth
63			img.set_pixel(ox + x, oy + 27, OUTLINE)
64	
65	
66	# Walk sheet (CHANGE-BRIEF.md §2): 4x1 cells of 64x80. The 56x72 scarecrow sits with its
67	# centre at the cell centre (offset 4, 4), so the pole foot is the bottom edge of the pole,
68	# the continuous point (32, 74) in each cell.
69	const WALK_CELL := Vector2i(64, 80)
70	const WALK_FOOT := Vector2(32.0, 74.0)
71	const WALK_LEAN_DEG := 5.0
72	# Per frame: lean (-1 left, 0 upright, +1 right) and y offset in px.
73	const WALK_POSES := [[0, 0], [-1, -3], [0, 1], [1, -3]]
74	
75	
76	func _scarecrow_walk() -> Image:
77		var upright := _blank(WALK_CELL.x, WALK_CELL.y)
78		_scarecrow_parts(upright, 4, 4)
79		var sheet := _blank(WALK_CELL.x * WALK_POSES.size(), WALK_CELL.y)
80		for i in WALK_POSES.size():
81			var cell := _walk_pose(upright, WALK_POSES[i][0], WALK_POSES[i][1])
82			sheet.blit_rect(_outlined(cell), Rect2i(Vector2i.ZERO, WALK_CELL), Vector2i(i * WALK_CELL.x, 0))
83		return sheet
84	
85	
86	## One pose: the flat upright parts rotated by lean * 5 degrees about the pole foot
87	## (nearest pixel, so the palette stays exact), then moved down by dy px.
88	## A negative angle in screen space (y down) tips the top to the left.
89	func _walk_pose(upright: Image, lean: int, dy: int) -> Image:
90		var cell := _blank(WALK_CELL.x, WALK_CELL.y)
91		var angle := deg_to_rad(WALK_LEAN_DEG) * lean
92		var c := cos(angle)
93		var s := sin(angle)
94		for y in WALK_CELL.y:
95			for x in WALK_CELL.x:
96				# Inverse map: this pixel's centre, un-moved and un-rotated, back to the upright pose.
97				var d := Vector2(x + 0.5, y - dy + 0.5) - WALK_FOOT
98				var src := WALK_FOOT + Vector2(d.x * c + d.y * s, -d.x * s + d.y * c)
99				var sx := floori(src.x)
100				var sy := floori(src.y)
101				if sx >= 0 and sy >= 0 and sx < WALK_CELL.x and sy < WALK_CELL.y:
102					var p := upright.get_pixel(sx, sy)
103					if p.a > 0.0:
104						cell.set_pixel(x, y, p)
105		return cell
106	
107	
108	func _archer() -> Image:
109		# Seen from behind and below: the archer faces up the screen, toward the enemies.
110		var img := _blank(44, 60)
111		_rect(img, 14, 46, 6, 12, LEATHER)         # legs
112		_rect(img, 24, 46, 6, 12, LEATHER)
113		_ellipse(img, 22, 36, 12, 13, HOOD)        # cloak
114		_rect(img, 10, 40, 24, 3, LEATHER)         # belt
115		_ellipse(img, 22, 16, 10, 11, HOOD)        # hood
116		_rect(img, 18, 24, 8, 4, SKIN)             # neck
117		_rect(img, 33, 4, 3, 44, BOW)              # bow stave
118		_rect(img, 36, 6, 1, 40, WHITE)            # bowstring
119		return _outlined(img)
120	
121	
122	func _arrow() -> Image:
123		var img := _blank(10, 30)
124		_rect(img, 4, 6, 2, 20, POLE)              # shaft
125		_rect(img, 3, 2, 4, 5, STEEL)              # head
126		_rect(img, 4, 0, 2, 3, FLAME)              # fire tip
127		_rect(img, 2, 24, 2, 5, FLETCH)            # fletching
128		_rect(img, 6, 24, 2, 5, FLETCH)
129		return _outlined(img)
130	
131	
132	func _mimi() -> Image:
133		var img := _blank(76, 60)
134		_rect(img, 6, 26, 64, 30, CHEST)           # chest body
135		_rect(img, 6, 6, 64, 14, LID)              # lid, raised a little: Mimi is peeking
136		_rect(img, 6, 20, 64, 6, OUTLINE)          # dark mouth gap
137		for x in range(10, 68, 8):                 # teeth
138			_rect(img, x, 20, 4, 3, WHITE)
139		_ellipse(img, 26, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)         # eyes on the lid
140		_ellipse(img, 50, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)
141		_rect(img, 25, 13, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
142		_rect(img, 49, 13, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
143		_rect(img, 14, 26, 5, 30, GOLD)            # gold bands
144		_rect(img, 57, 26, 5, 30, GOLD)
145		_rect(img, 33, 30, 10, 10, GOLD)           # lock
146		_rect(img, 37, 33, 2, 4, OUTLINE)
147		return _outlined(img)
148	
149	
150	func _blank(w: int, h: int) -> Image:
151		var img := Image.create(w, h, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
152		img.fill(Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
153		return img
154	
155	
156	func _rect(img: Image, x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int, c: Color) -> void:
157		img.fill_rect(Rect2i(x, y, w, h), c)
158	
159	
160	func _ellipse(img: Image, cx: int, cy: int, rx: int, ry: int, c: Color) -> void:
161		for y in range(cy - ry, cy + ry + 1):
162			for x in range(cx - rx, cx + rx + 1):
163				var dx := float(x - cx) / rx
164				var dy := float(y - cy) / ry
165				if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1.0 and x >= 0 and y >= 0 and x < img.get_width() and y < img.get_height():
166					img.set_pixel(x, y, c)
167	
168	
169	## Adds a 1-pixel dark outline around every opaque pixel (4-neighbour), in place.
170	func _outlined(img: Image) -> Image:
171		var src := img.duplicate() as Image
172		for y in img.get_height():
173			for x in img.get_width():
174				if src.get_pixel(x, y).a > 0.0:
175					continue
176				for d in [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1)]:
177					var p: Vector2i = Vector2i(x, y) + d
178					if p.x >= 0 and p.y >= 0 and p.x < img.get_width() and p.y < img.get_height() and src.get_pixelv(p).a > 0.0:
179						img.set_pixel(x, y, OUTLINE)
180						break
181		return img

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
set -o pipefail
mkdir -p logs
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
    fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
    fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
log="logs/$(basename "$1" .gd)_${tag}.log"
timeout "${3:-120}" godot --headless "${fps_args[@]}" --path godot --script "res://tests/$1" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
status=$?
if grep -qE "SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Failed loading resource" "$log"; then status=1; fi
exit $status

2	## Reads godot/assets/sprites/scarecrow_walk.png straight from disk (not through the importer)
3	## and checks the walk sheet against CHANGE-BRIEF.md §2: size, pole-foot registration,
4	## no clipping at any cell edge, and the scarecrow's colours in every cell.
5	##   bash scripts/run-test.sh test_scarecrow_sheet.gd 60
6	
7	const SHEET := "res://assets/sprites/scarecrow_walk.png"
8	const CELL_W := 64
9	const CELL_H := 80
10	const CELLS := 4
11	const Y_OFFSETS := [0, -3, 1, -3]   # brief §2 frame order, relative to frame 0
12	
13	# Source colours, the same values as godot/tools/make_sprites.gd.
14	const COLOURS := {
15		"STRAW": Color("e9c46a"),
16		"BURLAP": Color("d9b98a"),
17		"POLE": Color("8b5a2b"),
18		"HAT": Color("7a4e2d"),
19		"OUTLINE": Color("2b2b2b"),
20	}
21	
22	var failures := 0
23	
24	
25	func _init() -> void:
26		var img := Image.load_from_file(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(SHEET))
27		if img == null:
28			_check(false, "sheet loads from %s" % SHEET)
29			_finish()
30			return
31		img.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
32		_check(img.get_width() == CELL_W * CELLS and img.get_height() == CELL_H,
33			"sheet is 256x80 (got %dx%d)" % [img.get_width(), img.get_height()])
34	
35		# Pole foot: in each cell, the lowest row that holds any pixel of exactly the POLE colour
36		# (opaque, alpha 1) is the bottom of the pole; the foot's y is that row and its x is the
37		# midpoint of the leftmost and rightmost POLE pixels in that row. The x is kept doubled
38		# (min + max) so a half-pixel midpoint compares exactly as an integer.
39		var feet := []
40		for i in CELLS:
41			feet.append(_pole_foot(img, i))
42			print("cell %d: pole foot x2=%d (x=%.1f) y=%d" % [i, feet[i].x, feet[i].x / 2.0, feet[i].y])
43		for i in CELLS:
44			_check(feet[i].y >= 0, "cell %d has POLE pixels" % i)
45		if feet[0].y >= 0:
46			for i in range(1, CELLS):
47				_check(feet[i].x == feet[0].x,
48					"cell %d pole-foot x %.1f equals cell 0's %.1f" % [i, feet[i].x / 2.0, feet[0].x / 2.0])
49			for i in CELLS:
50				var want: int = feet[0].y + Y_OFFSETS[i]
51				_check(feet[i].y == want,
52					"cell %d pole-foot y %d equals cell 0's %d %+d = %d" % [i, feet[i].y, feet[0].y, Y_OFFSETS[i], want])
53	
54		for i in CELLS:
55			var edge := _edge_opaque_count(img, i)
56			_check(edge == 0, "cell %d: no opaque pixel on its outer row or column (found %d)" % [i, edge])
57	
58		for i in CELLS:
59			for name in COLOURS:
60				_check(_cell_has(img, i, COLOURS[name]), "cell %d contains %s" % [i, name])
61	
62		_finish()
63	
64	
65	func _pole_foot(img: Image, cell: int) -> Vector2i:
66		var pole: int = COLOURS["POLE"].to_rgba32()
67		for y in range(CELL_H - 1, -1, -1):
68			var lo := -1
69			var hi := -1
70			for x in CELL_W:
71				if img.get_pixel(cell * CELL_W + x, y).to_rgba32() == pole:
72					if lo < 0:
73						lo = x
74					hi = x
75			if lo >= 0:
76				return Vector2i(lo + hi, y)
77		return Vector2i(-1, -1)
78	
79	
80	func _edge_opaque_count(img: Image, cell: int) -> int:
81		var n := 0
82		for y in CELL_H:
83			for x in CELL_W:
84				if x != 0 and y != 0 and x != CELL_W - 1 and y != CELL_H - 1:
85					continue
86				if img.get_pixel(cell * CELL_W + x, y).a > 0.0:
87					n += 1
88		return n
89	
90	
91	func _cell_has(img: Image, cell: int, c: Color) -> bool:
92		var want := c.to_rgba32()
93		for y in CELL_H:
94			for x in CELL_W:
95				if img.get_pixel(cell * CELL_W + x, y).to_rgba32() == want:
96					return true
97		return false
98	
99	
100	func _check(ok: bool, what: String) -> void:
101		print("%s %s" % ["PASS" if ok else "FAIL", what])
102		if not ok:
103			failures += 1
104	
105	
106	func _finish() -> void:
107		print("RESULT %s (%d failure%s)" % ["PASS" if failures == 0 else "FAIL", failures, "" if failures == 1 else "s"])
108		quit(1 if failures > 0 else 0)
